page.layout: Running head and page number at the top: "PARS SECVNDA." at centre, "235" at right. Below them two engraved medallion portraits side by side, each with a legend around its rim. Below the portraits one column of running text in two paragraphs. Below the text a woodcut headpiece with no printed words.

main_text.l: CAROLVS Sabaudię Dux, ex antiqua ac illustri Saxo-
niæ familia oriundus, fratri suo Philiberto cognomine pulchro,
qui nulla relicta stirpe obierat, successit. Porrò anno à Christo
nato 1535. Carolus hic Allobrogum Ducatu, ac maxima Pede-
montii parte deturbatus est: nam urbes atque arces quampluri-
mas partim expugnat, partim in deditionem accepit Frācifcus
Valesius: tum quòd Gallicanis expeditionibus infestissima sem-
per hæc gens esset, tum quòd ius suum persequeretur in hæc ipsa
Sabaudiæ territoria. Vide Chro. Sabaudiæ, & Supplem. Chro.
BEATRIX Portugalliæ Regis filia, sorórque uxoris ipsius
Imperatoris Caroli quinti, liberali ac eleganti forma Princeps,
Carolo supradicto Duci nupsit, ex eóque Philiberti, qui Prin-
ceps Sabaudiæ vocatur, suscepit. Cęterùm hæc cùm deploratę
sibi in Sabaudia & Pedemontio res essent, Niciam concessit, ac
post paucos annos decessit. Vide Chron.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are read from the engraving and are not certain. The left-hand legend of the right medallion is doubtful. The woodcut headpiece below the text has no printed words. Printed "f" in long-s position is transcribed as s. Sabaudię keeps the ę as it appears on the scan.
